newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat as new issues dominate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat as new issues dominate.

text.p: Singapore shares opened almost unchanged on Tuesday with much of the activity again focused on recently listed shares, dealers said.
By 0140 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 3.57 points down at 2,189.84.

Top of the volume was Wee Poh Holdings, which debuted on Monday more than 80 percent above its initial public offer price of Singapore $0.45. By 0140 GMT, the stock was down four cents at at S$0.79 on profit-taking with 5.75 million shares traded.
Telephone monopoly Singapore Telecom (SingTel) also saw some profit-taking as it fell two cents to S$3.36.
SingTel's shares ran up 12 cents on Monday after the company reported a better than expected 13.6 percent increase in its first-half net profit last week.
Dealers said the STII could consolidate in the short-term and noted some chart analysts were predicting a fall towards 2,150 points before the index stabilised.
But others said many Singapore stocks were still relatively undervalued and predicted a rally towards 2,300 points as the end of the year approached.
"End-year window-dressing should help the market," said one.
